workflow: Enumerate source records and preserve source identifiers.
Reconcile works, editions, witnesses and commentaries without merging uncertain matches.
Find direct online text or scan links and compare provenance, completeness, access and accuracy.
Record language, script, format, edition, source, rights, link checks and evidence.
Choose a preferred source only after a documented comparison; record gaps and competing editions.
Independently review representative links, metadata and coverage before claiming completion.

Review first-release scope and source-specific rights.
Inventory local and online collections and reconcile works and editions without assuming completeness.
Convert approved source texts to source-aligned Markdown and validate against source.
Create passage-level IDs and reviewed alignments before indexing.
Test filters, search and source attribution with representative Hindu and Buddhist questions.

principles: Convert other source formats to UTF-8 Markdown with stable work, edition, passage and page or folio locators when available.
Preserve original wording, scripts, accents, variants, attribution and source alignment; mark uncertain OCR and missing material.
Keep machine-readable metadata and provenance alongside Markdown, including source URL, edition, rights, hash, conversion method, version, review status and locator mappings.
Retain authorized original source artifacts separately as evidence; the AI corpus uses Markdown. Do not assume conversion resolves reuse rights.
Split for retrieval at meaningful passage boundaries with context; never equate Markdown conversion with transcription accuracy.
canonical_corpus.search_note: Keyword, semantic retrieval and summarization are future capabilities, not implemented by this catalogue.

facet_policy.multi_valued: A work may belong to multiple traditions, collections, languages and topics; unknown is not none.
facet_policy.source_labels: Retain source labels and map them to normalized facets only with evidence and review.
facet_policy.topic_tags: Proposed discovery vocabulary; assignments are not authoritative without textual evidence.
facet_policy.language_script: Language, script and transliteration scheme are separate; record source-specific values per edition.
facet_policy.search: Index original and normalized titles, aliases, scripts and transliterations separately. Future semantic search must retrieve source-backed passages, with edition, access and provenance filters.
facet_policy.relations: Explicitly evidence commentary, translation and parallel links; do not infer identity from names or numbering.
facet_policy.migration: Version 2 moves works[].editions to top-level editions[], linked by work_id; IDs and edition evidence are retained.
facet_policy.filtering: Use contains for multi-value facets; an exact is filter may not match array values.
